The future of testing could give testers more room for the work that matters.
Kasturi Rajamanikkam
, Senior QA Engineer and AI enthusiast, believes AI can be a massive opportunity for the testing community.

From moving beyond coded automation to embracing codeless testing, to automating regression and smoke suites across 30+ CMS-based websites, Kasturi shares how her approach to automation has evolved with ACCELQ.

And with self-healing helping reduce maintenance, there’s more room for testers to focus on strategy, complex business logic, edge cases, and quality.
Because the goal isn’t to replace the tester.

It’s to give testers more time to do what they do best.

🎥 Hear Kasturi’s firsthand take on AI and the future of software testing.

4 signals your open-source test automation may be reaching its limit:

1️⃣ Maintenance is eating into coverage time
2️⃣ Your toolchain is becoming fragmented
3️⃣ Automation depends on a handful of specialists
4️⃣ CI/CD integration needs constant rework

If two or more are showing up consistently, it may be time to revisit your automation strategy.

Our latest blog explores the Maintenance Crossover Point and what comes next.
